title: Suggest Safety: Anti-Fake-Resolve Defense System
desc: 4-layer defense against fake bulk-resolves: git auto-commit on state change, pre-op snapshot, DataDir migration guard, suggest audit command
steps: Git auto-commit after every resolve/merge/submit (SuggestCommand.GitCommit.cs): chore(suggest): action ts
Pre-op snapshot before resolve/merge: suggestions.bak.{ts}.jsonl, 7d retention
DataDir migration guard on Eye start: copies suggestions.jsonl from legacy path if new DataDir empty
suggest audit: compares new vs legacy DataDir line counts, exit 1 on SPLIT-BRAIN

Git auto-commit BaseDirectory fix (2026-05-01, commit 7b3a1947): GitCommitSuggestFiles now walks up from AppContext.BaseDirectory (wkappbot exe dir) instead of caller CWD. Fixes 'outside repository' error when suggest is run from a different repo (e.g. WkAutoQuant). CWD of the binary exe always points to the WKAppBot repo.

SKILL SPLIT-BRAIN OWNER: WKAppBot maintainer owns all skill sync conflicts. After any commit that edits skills, run 'wkappbot skill sync' and resolve any conflicts immediately. Unresolved split-brain = peer repos run stale skill versions silently.

AutoRegisterBug as defensive instrumentation: whenever you write code that 'might not work as intended', plant AutoRegisterBug at the boundary. Examples: unexpected state (e.g. null where non-null expected), deprecated API usage detected at runtime, fallback path taken that should never fire in production, cross-thread race condition window, CDP/UIA response outside expected shape, user action that contradicts invariants. Pattern: if (suspiciousCondition) { AutoRegisterBug("[BUG-AUTO] <what was unexpected and where>"); } -- fires silently, no UI, survives exceptions. Already used in: a11y eval deprecated guard, CommandHelpMap miss, CDP pump failure, callout deny. Apply proactively when writing new code -- instrument first, debug later.
